title: Too Late Now
paragraphs: “The one who shot the poisoned needle looked completely dumbfounded, didn’t he?”
“There were also a few who kept trying to snipe Naofumi from a distance…”

“In my world, there’s an old foreign movie that came out before supernatural abilities were widely recognized. The protagonist is a superhuman, and… well, it was just like that. He casually took bullets without a scratch.”
When bullets hit Father, they simply fell harmlessly to the ground with a soft plop.
“If anything, we had a harder time than Naofumi did.”
“Yeah, since our enhancements aren’t complete yet, it still stings a little.”
“Feels about the same as getting shot with an airsoft gun.”
Ren and Itsuki say that while the bullets don’t pierce them, they do cause some slight pain. As for me? Thanks to my ability adjustments, I remain completely unharmed—just like Father.
“Sakura-chan and the others avoid getting hit altogether thanks to their feathers, so the only one really struggling was Éclair.”
“I can’t believe it… My duty is to protect the Heroes, yet I ended up being the one protected.”
“And those guys actually had the nerve to yell, ‘Die! Shield Demon and his band of false Heroes! We won’t let you reach Faubrey!’”
“They’re still coming after us? I mean, didn’t Motoyasu burn down the church? Their global authority should’ve been ruined, and yet they’re still so active. That’s kind of impressive.”
“Religion is deeply rooted, after all.”
Ren mutters, exasperated.
“How did you even take down the Three Heroes Church in the first timeline?”
“It was thanks to Father cleaning up after us in Melromarc while we ran around doing whatever we wanted. Because of that, the people started to see the Shield Hero in a positive light.”
“Then did some other faction force them to convert?”
I nod, but Ren and Itsuki tilt their heads in confusion.
“That’s… surprisingly simple.”
“But if the god they worship starts acting selfishly while the ‘devil’ they hate is the one offering them salvation, it’s only natural for them to question their beliefs.”
“Hmm… So in that strategy, the Heroes just ran wild as they pleased?”
“Exactly. In the previous loop, Ren and Itsuki ended up triggering the Four Guardian Beasts’ rampage as a result.”
“Still, I don’t like the idea of being manipulated by some conspiracy, sticking around Melromarc, and trying to work things out while trusting Naofumi.”
“Yeah, there’s no way I’d ever grovel to that dead king and princess, even in death.”
In the end, it has become an unspoken rule that we must leave Melromarc. Father always said he wouldn’t be able to stay there—and now we understand exactly why.
“If we try to maneuver things too carefully, the chances of getting found out are just too high. Cutting ties and leaving is the best option.”
“But then, just like now, the Three Heroes Church will keep coming after us…”
“Looks like wiping out a religion is a tall order, no matter which world you’re in.”
“And even in the first timeline, Naofumi struggled with remnants of the Three Heroes Church.”
“I wonder what’s happening in Melromarc now. Is the Three Heroes Church still active?”
“No idea… Even when checking with the guild, there haven’t been any major movements.”

There’s an eerie lack of information regarding Melromarc’s current situation. If anything, I expected at least some reports—maybe about Siltvelt invading after we took down Trash. But there’s been nothing. Something feels off.
“Well, either way, once we arrive in Faubrey and explain Melromarc’s outrageous actions, that’ll be the end of it.”
“The Three Heroes Church being evil—that’s the conclusion Itsuki wanted, huh?”
“I wouldn’t go that far. I just don’t want to fight for people who, even after all this, are still dreaming of a world that conveniently benefits them.”
“Naofumi, what’s for dinner?”
Sakura-chan has started pestering us about food.
“Just wait a little longer. We’re planning to eat at the inn tonight, and if we eat too early, you’ll be hungry again when it’s time to sleep.”
“Okay~”
Ren, Itsuki, and Éclair are watching the exchange. Meanwhile, Yuki-chan and the others are resting on the bed.
“You know, you actually get used to motion sickness after a while.”
“Yeah, at the start of the journey, I was really worried about it, but now it’s not a problem.”
“With how much we were being thrown around, I honestly thought I was gonna die from a brain hemorrhage.”
“I thought I was used to riding horses and Filolials, but that was on a whole other level.”
“At this point, I feel like I could handle riding on anything.”
“I think I’ve developed some serious resistance to motion sickness—kind of like Naofumi.”
“Not being able to enjoy that dizziness is a tragedy. You should be lamenting it.”
“Let’s just ignore Motoyasu. He’s completely in the masochist zone now.”
As we continue our conversation, Father strokes Sakura-chan’s head and then looks over at me.
“Once we arrive in Faubrey, Sakura-chan and the others will finally be able to Class Up, right?”
“Yeah. At this point, relying solely on potential growth is reaching its limit.”
“Agreed. They’ve gotten stronger, but even Éclair is starting to catch up now.”
“Once everyone Class Ups, I’ll probably be completely useless in battle.”
Huh? Éclair’s Class Up…? I feel like I’m forgetting something important. I’ve been putting off Yuki-chan and the others’ Class Ups until we get to Faubrey, knowing it won’t be a problem.
But why does something about this feel off? I feel like there was something I was told in the previous loop…
And this is something crucial for what’s ahead… Class Up…
“I remember now!”
“Whoa! What the hell?!”
I suddenly stand up, startling Father and the others.
“It’s about Class Ups!”
“Yeah, and? What about it?”
“Wasn’t the issue with Éclair’s ability supposed to be handled through improving her natural potential?”
“No, that’s not it. It’s about breaking the Class Up limit!”
“Huh? Isn’t Class Up only something you do at level 40?”
“In the game, you’d hit the cap at level 100, and after completing a quest, you could go beyond 100 by changing classes…”
“Yeah…”
Ren and Itsuki are explaining to Father and Éclair. Now that I think about it, that’s how it was. It’s something like a third-tier job. Well, it’s a bit different in nature, though.
“This is a Class Up that allows you to surpass Lv 100.”
“Huh? Does that mean there’s a reason we can’t do it?”
“Yeah… It exists in legends, but the method has been lost.”
“So that means people in this world can only go up to Lv 100? Though it seems that doesn’t apply to heroes…”
“Some demi-humans have higher limits, but that doesn’t mean they’re limitless. Kitamura-dono, could it be that in the future, the lost knowledge of breaking the level cap was restored?”
I nod firmly.

How could I have forgotten this? It’s an extremely important factor. Even if only the heroes get stronger, overcoming the future challenges will become increasingly difficult. Numbers are power. No matter how strong a hero is… there’s no guarantee that I won’t face a situation where I can’t handle things alone, just like in the previous loop. At the very least, I’ve determined that our allies should also be able to break their limits like the heroes. Father from the first world also placed great importance on breaking the Class Up limit. I can’t recall what exactly happened afterward due to the haze in my memory, but having more fighting power is always better. And because I forgot about this, we’ve fallen significantly behind. After all, the condition for breaking the Class Up limit is that.
“Then, we’re heading back to Melromarc immediately.”
“What!? Why do we have to go back to Melromarc now!?”
“We’re already right in front of Faubrey!”
“Exactly! We’re almost there—why do we need to return to that country?”
“Can’t we just wait until we arrive in Faubrey?”
Father and the others each voice their objections. What they’re saying is perfectly reasonable, but we’re out of time—we have to go back.
“Wait, is there some kind of material required for the Class Up that can only be found in Melromarc?”
“No, that’s not it.”
“Then what’s the reason?”
“The method to break the level cap can be obtained in Faubrey. However, the person who can decipher it is in Melromarc.”
Father and the others tilt their heads in confusion.
Ugh… this is frustrating.
“Uh, so basically, we need someone in Melromarc to help us?”
“Yes, that’s correct. Specifically, the Dragon Emperor in Melromarc—Filo-tan’s rival—needs to steal the knowledge from the Dragon Emperor in Faubrey who is keeping the Class Up method secret.”
“Steal knowledge? You’re skipping over the details, so it’s hard to understand…”
“So in any case, we need to recruit this Dragon Emperor guy… Can’t we do that somewhere other than Melromarc?”
